Assert-True (Wait-ForFlag -Path $flag) "holder process should acquire the lock"
    Assert-True (Test-JobLockBusy -Id "xproc") "a lock held by another process reports busy"
    $holder.WaitForExit(40000) | Out-Null
    Assert-True (-not (Test-JobLockBusy -Id "xproc")) "lock is free once the holder exits"

    # The 2026-07-27 case: the holder is killed outright rather than exiting cleanly.
    # Windows marks the mutex abandoned and the next waiter must be able to claim it,
    # otherwise one external kill would wedge the job permanently.
    $flag2 = Join-Path $tempRoot "held2.flag"
    $victim = Start-LockHolder -JobId "killed" -FlagPath $flag2 -HoldSeconds 120
    Assert-True (Wait-ForFlag -Path $flag2) "victim process should acquire the lock"
    Assert-True (Test-JobLockBusy -Id "killed") "victim holds the lock"
    Stop-Process -Id $victim.Id -Force
    $victim.WaitForExit(40000) | Out-Null
    Assert-True (-not (Test-JobLockBusy -Id "killed")) "an abandoned lock must be reclaimable, not wedged"

    # --- reconciler decision table -------------------------------------------
    $registry = Join-Path $tempRoot "jobs.json"
    $recLedger = Join-Path $tempRoot "rec-ledger.json"
    $recLog = Join-Path $tempRoot "rec.log"
    @{
        version = 1
        jobs    = @(
            @{ id = "due-missing"; label = "due"; exe = "pwsh"; script = "{REPO}\scripts\morning-cadence.ps1"
                schedule = @{ kind = "daily"; at = "00:01" }; graceMinutes = 0; timeoutMinutes = 5
                maxAttemptsPerDay = 3; reconcile = $true
                successProbe = @{ kind = "fileContains"; path = $recLog; pattern = "done" } },
            @{ id = "not-due"; label = "later"; exe = "pwsh"; script = "{REPO}\scripts\morning-cadence.ps1"
                schedule = @{ kind = "daily"; at = "23:59" }; graceMinutes = 30; timeoutMinutes = 5
                maxAttemptsPerDay = 3; reconcile = $true },
            @{ id = "monitor-only"; label = "off"; exe = "pwsh"; script = "{REPO}\scripts\morning-cadence.ps1"
                schedule = @{ kind = "daily"; at = "00:01" }; graceMinutes = 0; timeoutMinutes = 5
                maxAttemptsPerDay = 3; reconcile = $false }
        )
    } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $registry -Encoding UTF8

    $reconcile = Join-Path $repoRoot "scripts\keystone-reconcile.ps1"
    $decide = {
        param($RegPath, $LedPath)
        $json = & $reconcile -DryRun -Json -RegistryPath $RegPath -LedgerPath $LedPath
        ($json | ConvertFrom-Json)
    }

    $d = & $decide $registry $recLedger
    $byJob = @{}; foreach ($x in $d) { $byJob[$x.job] = $x.action }
    Assert-Equal "make-up" $byJob["due-missing"] "an overdue job with no success must be made up"
    Assert-Equal "skip" $byJob["not-due"] "a job inside its grace period must be left alone"
    Assert-Equal "skip" $byJob["monitor-only"] "reconcile=false must never be run"

    # once the probe matches, the same job is left alone - this is what stops a
    # made-up briefing from sending a duplicate email
    Set-Content -LiteralPath $recLog -Value "done" -Encoding UTF8
    $d2 = & $decide $registry $recLedger
    $byJob2 = @{}; foreach ($x in $d2) { $byJob2[$x.job] = $x.action }
    Assert-Equal "skip" $byJob2["due-missing"] "a job whose probe reports success must not be re-run"

    # attempt cap
    Remove-Item -LiteralPath $recLog -Force
    Add-LedgerEntry -Id "due-missing" -Status "failed" -ExitCode 1 -Path $recLedger | Out-Null
    Add-LedgerEntry -Id "due-missing" -Status "failed" -ExitCode 1 -Path $recLedger | Out-Null
    Add-LedgerEntry -Id "due-missing" -Status "failed" -ExitCode 1 -Path $recLedger | Out-Null
    $d3 = & $decide $registry $recLedger
    $byJob3 = @{}; foreach ($x in $d3) { $byJob3[$x.job] = $x.action }
    Assert-Equal "give-up" $byJob3["due-missing"] "the attempt cap must stop an endless retry loop"

    # --- shipped registry sanity --------------------------------------------
    $realJobs = Get-JobRegistry
    Assert-True ($realJobs.Count -ge 1) "data\jobs.json must define jobs"
    foreach ($j in $realJobs) {
        Assert-True ([bool]$j.id) "every job needs an id"
        $target = Expand-JobToken -Value $j.script
        Assert-True (Test-Path -LiteralPath $target) "job '$($j.id)' script must exist: $target"
        Assert-True (Test-ScheduledOn -Job $j -Date $mon) "schedule kind must be understood for '$($j.id)'"
        $null = Get-ScheduledDateTime -Job $j -Date $mon

content.content:
<#
  Runs a managed job (see data\jobs.json) and records the outcome to the run ledger.

  This is the only place a managed job should be started from. Both the scheduled task
  and the reconciler go through here, and the per-job mutex is what keeps them from
  ever running the same job twice at once.

  Exit codes: 0 = job succeeded or was already running, 1 = job failed/timed out.
#>
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Job,
    [ValidateSet("scheduled", "reconcile", "manual")][string]$Trigger = "scheduled",
    [switch]$MadeUp,
    [string]$RegistryPath,
    [string]$LedgerPath
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
. (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "run-ledger.ps1")

$def = Get-JobDefinition -Id $Job -RegistryPath $RegistryPath
$scriptPath = Expand-JobToken -Value $def.script

if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $scriptPath)) {
    Add-LedgerEntry -Id $def.id -Status "failed" -ExitCode 127 -Trigger $Trigger -MadeUp:$MadeUp `
        -Note "script not found: $scriptPath" -Path $LedgerPath | Out-Null
    Write-Error "Job '$Job': script not found at $scriptPath"
    exit 1
}

# Working directory: an explicit override, else the project root (the parent of a
# 'scripts' folder), else the script's own directory.
if ($def.PSObject.Properties['workingDirectory'] -and $def.workingDirectory) {
    $workDir = Expand-JobToken -Value $def.workingDirectory
} else {
    $scriptDir = Split-Path -Parent $scriptPath
    $workDir = if ((Split-Path -Leaf $scriptDir) -eq 'scripts') { Split-Path -Parent $scriptDir } else { $scriptDir }
}

switch ($def.exe) {
    'pwsh' {
        $pwshCmd = Get-Command pwsh -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        $exePath = if ($pwshCmd) { $pwshCmd.Source } else { '/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh' }
        $exeArgs = @('-NoProfile', '-File', $scriptPath)
    }
    'powershell' {
        $exePath = "/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh"
        $exeArgs = @('-NoProfile', '-ExecutionPolicy', 'Bypass', '-File', $scriptPath)
    }
    'bash' {
        $exePath = '/bin/bash'
        $exeArgs = @($scriptPath)
    }
    'cmd' {
        $exePath = "$env:SystemRoot\System32\cmd.exe"
        $exeArgs = @('/c', $scriptPath)
    }
    default { throw "Job '$Job': unsupported exe '$($def.exe)'." }
}

$logDir = Join-Path (Get-KeystoneRoot) "outputs/jobs"
if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $logDir)) { New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $logDir | Out-Null }
$stamp = (Get-Date).ToString("yyyy-MM-dd")
$outLog = Join-Path $logDir "$($def.id)-$stamp.out.log"
$errLog = Join-Path $logDir "$($def.id)-$stamp.err.log"

$result = Invoke-WithMutex -Name "job-$($def.id)" -TimeoutMs 0 -SkipIfBusy -Body {
    $startedAt = Get-Date
    Write-Host "[$($startedAt.ToString('HH:mm:ss'))] job '$($def.id)' starting ($Trigger)"

    $proc = Start-Process -FilePath $exePath -ArgumentList $exeArgs `
        -WorkingDirectory $workDir -PassThru `
        -RedirectStandardOutput $outLog -RedirectStandardError $errLog

    $timeoutMs = [int]$def.timeoutMinutes * 60 * 1000
    if (-not $proc.WaitForExit($timeoutMs)) {
        try { $proc.Kill($true) } catch { }
        $finishedAt = Get-Date
        Add-LedgerEntry -Id $def.id -Status "timeout" -ExitCode 258 -StartedAt $startedAt `
            -FinishedAt $finishedAt -Trigger $Trigger -MadeUp:$MadeUp `
            -Note "exceeded $($def.timeoutMinutes)m" -Path $LedgerPath | Out-Null
        Write-Warning "job '$($def.id)' timed out after $($def.timeoutMinutes)m"
        return 1
    }

    $finishedAt = Get-Date
    $code = $proc.ExitCode

    # 0xC000013A (STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT) means the process was terminated rather than
    # having failed on its own - a Restart Manager shutdown during an MSI upgrade is
    # the case that motivated this system. Recorded distinctly so it stays diagnosable.
    $status = if ($code -eq 0) { "ok" }
    elseif ($code -eq -1073741510 -or $code -eq 3221225786) { "killed" }
    else { "failed" }

    $note = if ($status -eq 'killed') { "terminated externally (0xC000013A)" } else { $null }
    Add-LedgerEntry -Id $def.id -Status $status -ExitCode $code -StartedAt $startedAt `
        -FinishedAt $finishedAt -Trigger $Trigger -MadeUp:$MadeUp -Note $note -Path $LedgerPath | Out-Null

    Write-Host "[$($finishedAt.ToString('HH:mm:ss'))] job '$($def.id)' -> $status (exit $code, $([int]($finishedAt-$startedAt).TotalSeconds)s)"
    if ($status -eq 'ok') { return 0 } else { return 1 }
}

if ($null -eq $result) {
    Write-Host "job '$($def.id)' is already running - nothing to do."
    exit 0
}
exit $result

# Decisions Log

Append meaningful KeystoneOS decisions here.

## 2026-06-09 - Create KeystoneOS

Decision: Build `KeystoneOS` as a local control-plane repo under `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\KeystoneOS`, then push it as a private GitHub repo once the MVP skeleton is committed.

Rationale:

- DEV already contains the active coding projects KeystoneOS must coordinate.
- SecondBrain should remain the human synthesis vault, not the operating repo.
- Existing Claude and Codex memory systems should be preserved and integrated by reference.
- A private repo is appropriate because KeystoneOS contains local paths, memory pointers, project context, and operational details.

## 2026-06-09 - Keep Graphify Controlled

Decision: Store durable Graphify outputs repo-locally in `<project>\graphify-out`, and use `SecondBrain\Projects\Graphify\<ProjectKey>\GRAPHIFY_SYNC.md` as the Obsidian-facing bridge.

Rationale:

- Project graphs should remain close to the source code they describe.
- Obsidian should receive controlled manifests and project-facing graph notes, not unmanaged generated node dumps.
- The first KeystoneOS graph refresh produced an AST-only graph with 61 nodes, 140 edges, and 11 communities at `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\KeystoneOS\graphify-out`.

## 2026-06-10 - Keep the Control Center File-Backed

Decision: Extend the daily cockpit with generated action-plan and closeout packets instead of introducing a persistent server or database.

Rationale:

- KeystoneOS is still early MVP infrastructure, and the highest-value gap is operational continuity, not a heavier app shell.
- Static markdown and HTML outputs preserve the repo's role as a map/control plane while keeping canonical project files in their source repos.
- `plan` turns live registry, git, graph, intake, and handoff signals into the next-action surface.
- `closeout` captures changed files, latest generated artifacts, restart commands, and verification expectations before the session ends.

## 2026-06-11 - Map, Don't Copy (Other-Worlds Decision)

Decision: Adopt the Nate Herk video's router and cadence patterns, but reject per-domain vault duplication ("other worlds"). DEV projects integrate into KeystoneOS by registry promotion (`keystone.ps1 promote`), never by copying or moving files in.

Rationale:

- Canonical sources stay in their repos; KeystoneOS links and briefs point at them.
- Duplication creates sync drift across harnesses and breaks per-project git history.
- Source: `outputs/yt-8QQ_INxAhRs-transcript.txt`; synthesis note at `SecondBrain/Knowledge/frameworks/claude-code-second-brain.md`.

## 2026-06-12 - Federation, Made Operational (not a monorepo)

Decision: Keep KeystoneOS as a federated control plane over projects that stay in their own repos. Reject physical consolidation / monorepo. Deliver the "one command center" experience in the orchestration layer: self-healing path resolution, ownership/visibility metadata, and one-hop context auto-load.

Rationale:

- token-dashboard is borrowed and public-bound; cannot be vendored into a private monorepo, and a subfolder of a private repo cannot be selectively published.
- SecondBrain is in scope but is an Obsidian vault that cannot live inside a code repo without breaking Obsidian sync. A monorepo therefore cannot even hold "everything."
- "Single entry point, full context, operate on anything" are orchestration properties, not disk-layout ones — the harness already reaches any absolute path on the machine.
- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-12-operational-command-center.md`; plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-12-operational-command-center.md`.

## 2026-06-12 - OKR-Driven Cockpit (command-center slice 1)

Decision: The KeystoneOS command center is built OKR-first. Slice 1 = the morning cockpit (`outputs/dashboard/cockpit.html`): an OKR scoreboard hero (read from okr-tracker's generated `okrs.json`), a derived "start here today" triage, project lanes grouped by the KR they serve (via the `okr` tag on projects, set with `okr-link`), and an ad-hoc quick-start lane. Token-spend, skills, and agents panels are deferred (roadmap M2-M5).

Rationale:

- OKRs should get daily attention; making them the cockpit hero puts them front-and-center every morning. Each KR's next_action/blocker IS the triage signal.
- okr-tracker stays the single source of truth; KeystoneOS consumes its `okrs.json` (additive `--json` export), never reinventing OKR logic or writing into `okrs.yaml`.
- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-12-okr-cockpit-design.md`; plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-12-okr-cockpit.md`.

## 2026-07-23 - Durability layer: everything backed up, git only where it earns it

Decision: Full-system audit (7/23) found capture healthy but durability broken. Remediation shipped same day, two phases:

- Phase 1: every knowledge store got a private GitHub remote under erash11 - SecondBrain (212 outstanding files pushed), `dotclaude` (~\.claude config, whitelist .gitignore), `claude-skills`, `claude-global-memory`, morning-briefing, ZoteroInjestion; claude-memory-compiler forked (origin=erash11 fork, upstream=coleam00) so local patches are pushable.
- Phase 2: scheduled task `KeystoneOS-DailyBackup` (daily 06:15) runs `~\.claude\scripts\daily-backup.ps1` - auto-commits+pushes the four memory repos and robocopy-snapshots non-git stores. Stack doctor gained `backup-*` issue codes. Restore runbook: `~\.claude\RESTORE.md` (dotclaude repo - first repo cloned on a new machine).

Rationale:

- No mono-repo, and no git-repo-for-everything: git for code/text that evolves; robocopy snapshots for data-heavy folders (non-repo DEV dirs -> Baylor OneDrive `Backups\DEV-NonRepo`).
- Sensitivity split: personal context (Claude transcripts `~\.claude\projects`, Codex/Gemini state) snapshots to personal GOOGLE DRIVE (`G:\My Drive\Backups\Machine`) - the personal OneDrive account was found not signed in (dead folder), and the gmail account is the durable personal identity; never Baylor storage; Baylor work folders snapshot to Baylor OneDrive.
- Automation never merges: a diverged memory repo is escalated to `.errors.log`, not auto-merged.
- Deliberately unprotected: `~\.codex\work` (19+ GB of clones), Milvus index (rebuildable), credentials.

## 2026-07-24 - OS audit: routing and freshness drift closed, drift guard added

Decision: Installed the `os-audit` skill (`.claude/skills/os-audit/SKILL.md`) and ran the first full six-check drift audit. Report: `audits/os-audit-2026-07-24.md`. Applied fix batches A-D.

Finding that shaped everything else: **cadence was healthy, claims were not.** Every cron-driven surface (inventory, morning, dashboard, agy, codex-hooks, daily backup) was current through 2026-07-24 and all four scheduled tasks returned 0. Every hand-written surface had frozen on 2026-06-09/06-12 and had been quietly lying to agents for ~45 days. Four checks came back RED against a system that looked well-maintained.

Applied:

- Routing: `CLAUDE.md` pointed at `CONTEXT.md` + `docs/adr/`, neither of which exists — repointed at `decisions/log.md`, the actual ADR store. Added `memory/`, `knowledge/`, `connections.md`, `.scratch/`, `audits/`, `data/memory-index-paths.json`, and `context/standing-rules.md` to the AGENTS.md table.
- **Precedence rule added to AGENTS.md** — five lines declaring what wins when two stores disagree (AGENTS.md over other routers; generated over hand-written; live check over recorded state; root over worktree; newest decision wins). Its absence was the root cause of every clash finding.
- Poisoning removed at source, by making the files structurally incapable of going stale rather than by refreshing them: `connections.md` rewritten as capability + check-command (its "gh token invalid" row had been false for weeks); `graphify/registry.md` drops snapshot node/edge counts and 3 phantom paths; `memory/sources.md` collapsed to a pointer at `data/memory-sources.json` (it said 6 sources, the JSON said 7).
- `context/standing-rules.md` created — cross-harness rules (PowerShell-over-Bash, one-pipeline-run-at-a-time, atomic .rds writes, reviews-check-unmerged-PRs, Fireflies-CLI-first, Zotero read-only) that previously existed only in Claude-side memory and `.scratch/`, invisible to Codex and Gemini. This is the gap KeystoneOS exists to close.
- Bloat: removed 3 merged worktrees (611 duplicate files of AGENTS.md/registry/scripts at older commits — verified content-identical to main first; branches preserved). `phase2-durability` kept per Eric and now `git worktree lock`ed with a reason so the intent is machine-readable. Deleted a junk tree literally named `C:` (the colon stored as U+F03A, Windows' escape for an illegal path char, which is why every normal path API reported it absent). Re-homed `tezino-pulse-check.png` and `.ecc-design/` into `outputs/presentation/`. Labelled `knowledge/` as a retired June snapshot.
- `.gitignore`: `.claude/worktrees/`, `jobs/`, `shell-snapshots/`, `todos/` ignored; `.claude/skills/` now tracked so installed skills are versioned and covered by the backup layer. (`settings.local.json` stays excluded by global gitignore — intentional.)
- Durability: new `scripts/os-freshness.ps1` + `keystone freshness [-Sweep]`, wired into the morning cadence. Checks hand-written surface age (30-day budget), routing integrity, unmapped folders, root hygiene, merged worktrees, and audit cadence (90-day budget).

Rationale:

- The fix for a stale fact in an always-loaded file is a pointer, not a fresher copy. A fresher copy just resets the clock on the same failure.
- `health` answers "do paths resolve"; nothing answered "are the claims still true." That second question is the one that decays silently, so it needed its own check and its own cadence.
- A check that cries wolf gets ignored: the drift guard only judges paths this repo owns, and treats a locked worktree as a deliberate keep rather than a finding.
- Deliberately not fixed here: `memsearch` indexing is timing out (`ETIMEDOUT` 5x consecutively, `~\.claude\global-memory\transcripts\.errors.log`), degrading L1 memory retrieval. Outside this repo; belongs to `/claude-stack-doctor`. Recorded in `context/priorities.md` as an open thread.

Verification: test suite 22/23 (the one failure, `skill-verification-contracts.ps1`, is the documented pre-existing `argument-hint` key in `~/.agents/skills/diagram-generator`, outside this repo, and fails identically on main). `keystone health` clean, 17/17 project paths resolve. `keystone freshness` clean. Next deep audit due 2026-10-24.

## 2026-07-27 - Reconcile jobs against a run ledger, not against the scheduler

Decision: Managed jobs are declared in `data/jobs.json`, started only through `scripts\run-job.ps1`, and recorded in `outputs\run-ledger.json`. `scripts\keystone-reconcile.ps1` (task `KeystoneOS-Reconcile`, at logon +5m and hourly) re-runs anything with no success recorded for today. Supporting: `RestartCount = 2` on the pwsh tasks, a `PT10M` random start delay, and `KeystoneOS-StackDoctor` moved from Mon 06:40 to Mon 10:30.

Rationale:

- The morning cadence did not run on 2026-07-27, and nothing noticed. It was found because a human asked.
- Three causes stacked, and the important point is that they were *different* causes with one shared consequence:
  - The machine shut down unexpectedly at 22:03 on 07-26 and stayed down, so 06:00 and 06:15 were missed outright.
  - `StartWhenAvailable` fired every catch-up run at the identical second, 07:54:28, ~8 minutes after boot — directly into Windows Update, Defender, Secure Boot key rotation and WER crash uploads.
  - At 07:57:07 a `winget upgrade --id Microsoft.PowerShell` began; the 7.6.4 MSI's Restart Manager named `pwsh.exe` pid 9864 — the running cadence — and shut it down at 07:57:46. Application log events 10010/10002 are explicit about this.
- `StartWhenAvailable` was already this repo's fix for an earlier instance of the same class (see the comment in `install-morning-cadence-task.ps1`). It handles *missed trigger* and cannot handle *started, then died* — so the class kept recurring in a new shape. Adding a third point fix would have repeated that mistake.
- Reconciling against recorded outcome is cause-agnostic: shutdown, crash, external kill and transient failure all reduce to "no success recorded today", and all get the same make-up. The failure mode becomes "ran late" instead of "never ran, nobody knew".
- Every KeystoneOS task had `RestartCount = 0`. One kill lost the whole day. `KeystoneOS-StackDoctor` — the watchdog — was itself scheduled Mondays 06:40, inside the window it exists to inspect.
- `successProbe` reads a job's own log, so a job not routed through `run-job.ps1` is still judged correctly. This is what stops a made-up `morning-briefing` from sending a duplicate email.

Rejected: stored-credential (`Password`) logon so tasks run without an interactive session. On a Baylor-managed device the password rotates, and each rotation would silently break every task — trading a rare failure for a recurring one.

Verified: `tests\keystone-reconcile.ps1` passes (schedule matching, probe evaluation, ledger round-trip, corrupt-ledger recovery, cross-process locking, abandoned-mutex reclaim, attempt cap, decision table). Live, the reconciler independently rediscovered all four job states, including the Outlook auth warning; `run-job.ps1` ran `stack-doctor` and `morning-cadence` to `ok` and the reconciler then correctly skipped both.

Still open — a *separate* bug, not addressed here: `KeystoneOS-DailyBackup` exited `0xC000013A` at 07:56:56, **11 seconds before winget started**, writing zero lines to `daily-backup.log`. That is the same signature as 07-25 and 07-26 above, which the credential-helper removal was meant to fix. It recurred, so that fix was incomplete. The reconciler now makes the run up and the attempt cap writes to `.errors.log`, but the underlying cause is still unidentified.

## 2026-07-28 - Evict Projects From outputs/ Into DEV

Decision: `outputs/presentation/` and `outputs/website/` were projects living inside
the control plane. Both were moved out to their own top-level DEV folders and backed
up as private GitHub repos, so `outputs/` is now generated artifacts only.

- `outputs/presentation/` (32 files) -> `DEV\RTP_DataCollection_Talk` -> `erash11/RTP_DataCollection_Talk`
- `outputs/website/` (22 files) -> `DEV\Website` -> `erash11/AppliedPerformance-Site`

Both promoted into the registry; `health` reports 19/19 paths resolving, none drifted.

Rationale:

- This violated the founding rule in `AGENTS.md`: "KeystoneOS is a map and control
  plane, not the source repo for every project." A deck and a landing page are source,
  not output.
- The real damage was silent. `.gitignore` line 2 is `outputs/**`, with per-directory
  negations for the generated dirs. `presentation/` was never negated, and `website/`
  negated only the directory, not its contents. Net effect: **53 of 54 files had no
  copy anywhere but this laptop** — including `Pres_Script_v3_07082026.docx` and
  `RTP-Data-Collection-SCRIPT.md`, both edited 2026-07-08. The folder that looked
  most "inside the system" was the least protected thing in the repo.
- Generalized: storing a project under a path whose entire subtree is gitignored turns
  the backup rule into a silent data-loss trap. The gitignore was correct for outputs;
  the mistake was putting non-output there.
- Sequence used was copy -> push -> verify remote tree (32/32 and 22/22 files) -> only
  then delete sources, because the source was the only copy in existence.
- No breaking change: a grep of every `.ps1`/`.md`/`.json`/`.yml` in the repo found no
  script, skill, job, or routing-table reference to either path. The one live pointer,
  `CODEX_HANDOFF.md`'s "Where the files live", was updated in the new repo.

Boundary: `knowledge/baylor-01-ongoing/` was left alone — it is a retired Graphify
snapshot, already labelled as such, and is tracked (4/5 files), not a project.
`.scratch/speedprofiling*` also stays; that is the designed issue-tracker location
per `CLAUDE.md`.


## 2026-10-23 - daily-backup is monitor-only in reconcile

Decision: `data/jobs.json` sets `daily-backup` to `"reconcile": false`. Reconcile still lists it
("monitor-only") but never starts it.

Rationale:

- Since 2026-10-22 launchd runs the backup hourly 12:00-17:00 and at login, always through the gate
  `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup-login.sh` (AC power, none running, no OK today, max 2 tries).
- Reconcile's RunAtLoad at a login inside the 12:00-20:00 make-up window called `run-job.ps1`, which
  starts `daily-backup.ps1` directly and skips every gate check, so it could run on battery or start
  a second backup beside a gated one.
- Pointing reconcile at the gate was rejected: the gate exits 0 when it skips, and `run-job.ps1`
  would record that skip as a successful run.
- Trade-off: nothing retries between 17:00 and 20:00.

## 2026-08-02 - Durability work sequenced behind ownership, recovery, and data safety

Decision: Adopt the revised durability plan in
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-02-durability-contract-and-ownership.md` and build it in
that order. Resource controls (backpressure, watchdog, idle shutdown) are explicitly
deferred until after ownership, capture durability, and backup verification are proven.

- Sequence: (1) policy matrix / SLOs / job state model / baseline tests, (2) process
  ownership — run IDs, receipts, Job Object containment, lease identity, (3) separate
  `backup` from `index` from `verify-backup`, (4) durable coalesced worker, (5)
  observability and fault injection, (6) only then resource controls.
- Explicitly deferred, as decisions rather than oversights: a new permanent watchdog,
  aggressive CPU/RAM backpressure, idle shutdown, broad unattended automation, and any
  "exactly once" guarantee.

Rationale:

- The earlier plan started at symptoms. Five independent adversarial reviews converged
  on the same finding: backpressure, watchdogs, and idle shutdown were being added on
  top of an ownership model that had never been proven, which would have produced new
  failure modes while masking the existing ones.
- Identity, not liveness, is the missing primitive. A lease must carry PID + process
  start time + boot identity + a random owner token; PID alone is not identity, and PID
  reuse across a reboot is a live failure path today.
- Success must be a receipt, not an inference. Exit code, timestamp, and matching log
  text can all be produced by a run that did nothing — this applies to backups
  (run-specific completion receipt, periodic restore test) and to indexing (acknowledge
  only after a unique sentinel is actually searchable).
- Backups must be versioned/immutable snapshots, not mirrors. A mirror faithfully
  replicates the deletion you are trying to recover from.
- `tests/memsearch-concurrency.ps1` is five `Contains()` assertions against source
  strings — it spawns no processes and cannot fail for any concurrency reason. It is
  replaced by real fault injection, not extended.
- Session freshness is drift, not age. "Older than X" is replaced by a resume
  fingerprint (workspace, branch/HEAD, dirty state, harness version, hook generation,
  pending work): old-but-unchanged stays usable, recent-but-drifted warns or blocks.

This extends rather than replaces the 2026-07-27 run-ledger + reconciler design, which
stands; it widens the same idea from scheduled jobs to every job, hook, and backup.

# tests/run-job-inventory-row.ps1
# An inventory row in data/jobs.json (no timeoutMinutes; launchd starts it directly) must be
# refused by run-job.ps1 before anything starts: no process, no ledger entry, no job logs.
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
function Assert-True($Condition, $Message) { if (-not $Condition) { throw $Message } }

$repoRoot = Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..")
$tempRoot = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ("keystone-runjob-inv-test-" + [System.Guid]::NewGuid().ToString("n"))
$id = "inv-" + [System.Guid]::NewGuid().ToString("n").Substring(0, 8)
try {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $tempRoot | Out-Null
    $flag = Join-Path $tempRoot "started.flag"
    $script = Join-Path $tempRoot "job.sh"
    Set-Content -LiteralPath $script -Value "touch '$flag'" -Encoding UTF8
    $registry = Join-Path $tempRoot "jobs.json"
    $ledger = Join-Path $tempRoot "ledger.json"
    @{
        version = 1
        jobs    = @(@{ id = $id; label = "inventory"; exe = "bash"; script = $script
                       schedule = @{ kind = "daily"; at = "00:01" }; reconcile = $false })
    } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 | Set-Content -LiteralPath $registry -Encoding UTF8

    $runJob = Join-Path $repoRoot "scripts/run-job.ps1"
    $pwsh = (Get-Process -Id $PID).Path
    & $pwsh -NoProfile -File $runJob -Job $id -Trigger manual -RegistryPath $registry -LedgerPath $ledger 2>$null | Out-Null
    $code = $LASTEXITCODE

    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500
    Assert-True ($code -ne 0) "run-job must fail on an inventory row (exit $code)"
    Assert-True (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $flag)) "run-job must not start an inventory row's script"
    Assert-True (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $ledger)) "run-job must not write a ledger entry for an inventory row"
    $stamp = (Get-Date).ToString("yyyy-MM-dd")
    Assert-True (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $repoRoot "outputs/jobs/$id-$stamp.out.log"))) "run-job must not open job logs for an inventory row"

    Write-Host "run-job inventory-row test passed"
}
finally {
    if (Test-Path $tempRoot) { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $tempRoot -Recurse -Force }
}

cd ~/DEV/KeystoneOS && cat >> decisions/log.md <<'EOF'

## 2026-10-24 - jobs.json lists every loaded launchd job; the new rows are inventory only

Decision: `data/jobs.json` has a row for each of the 15 loaded `com.keystone` LaunchAgents. A new
`launchd` field names the label(s) behind each row (`daily-backup` carries both `dailybackup` and
`dailybackup-login`, which run the same gate script). The 11 new rows have `reconcile: false` and no
`timeoutMinutes`. `run-job.ps1` now refuses a row without `timeoutMinutes`.

Rationale:

- The registry knew 3 of 15 jobs, so "what runs on this Mac" had no answer in one place.
- Regenerating the registry was deferred on 10-23 because reconcile reads it and could start
  make-up runs. `reconcile: false` is checked before any schedule logic, so a new row can only ever
  be reported "monitor-only". Proved with `keystone-reconcile.ps1 -DryRun -Json` against the
  candidate file before it replaced the real one: 14 decisions, all `skip`.
- Schedules mirror the plists, including kinds reconcile does not understand (`monthly`,
  `interval`, `alsoAt`, `atLoad`). If such a row is ever flipped to `reconcile: true`, it fails
  closed as "not scheduled today" instead of running at a wrong time.
- Without `timeoutMinutes`, `run-job.ps1` would start the process and then throw under strict
  mode, leaving it running unsupervised and unrecorded (reproduced against the pre-change script).
  The guard refuses before anything starts. Test: `tests/run-job-inventory-row.ps1`.
- `tests/keystone-reconcile.ps1` now checks schedules only for reconciled rows. That test still stops
  at line 165 on macOS (`Start-Process -WindowStyle`), before the registry checks; the same checks
  were run on their own against the new file.
EOF
